description: Repair match_items(predicted, reference) so duplicate rows and interacting name/amount matches obey the one-to-one optimization contract. Inputs have at most eight rows each.
requirements: Rows are dicts with optional name (str or None) and amount (number, numeric string or None). Normalize names by collapsing whitespace and case-folding; only a nonempty normalized name can match.

An edge is eligible when nonempty normalized names match OR both amounts are finite, valid numeric values equal after Decimal(str(value)) rounding to 0.01 with ROUND_HALF_UP. None, booleans, invalid strings and nonfinite amounts never form amount edges.
Choose a one-to-one matching that first maximizes pair count, then maximizes the number of pairs with matching names. A name match does not outrank a larger number of pairs.
Break remaining ties by the lexicographically smallest sequence of (reference_index, predicted_index), ordered by reference index.
Return {'pairs': [(predicted_index, reference_index), ...], 'unmatched_predicted': [...], 'unmatched_reference': [...]}. Pairs are ordered by reference index and unmatched indices ascend.
Preserve duplicate row identities by index, preserve both input lists/dicts unchanged, and handle empty lists.

provenance.description: One-to-one line-item evaluation is a real concern in the previously studied document-processing task pool. The objective, bounded size, tie rules and all code/tests here are newly constructed; this is not a reproduction of a production defect.

validity_limits: Calibration only; these tasks do not establish representative development performance or generality.
Hidden tests are independent of the solving run, not independently authored from this fixture's reference implementation.
The oracle is one valid implementation, not an exact patch requirement; behavioral alternatives are allowed.
Passing visible tests is intentionally insufficient. Base failure is seeded and does not predict model failure rate.
